question: What is the carbon percentage by mass in the human body?
solution:
The correct answer is **__18.5%__****__.__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The **crucial atom **for organic chemistry is **carbon**, which has four places for atoms to bond with one another.
 
• **Proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, **and **lipids** are all **composed **of carbon chains.
 
• **Carbon-based bonds** can be **broken **to **release energy**.
 
• The average human body contains **18.5% carbon.**
 
• Most of the body's **cells **are composed** **primarily of **carbon.**
 
• It facilitates **cellular respiration**, a process by which the body releases glucose-stored energy. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• There are several methods for analyzing **body composition.**
 
• This can be done by looking at the molecular types present, such as **water, protein, fats (or lipids), hydroxylapatite (found in bones), carbohydrates (such glycogen and glucose), **and **DNA, **or by the chemical elements that are present.
 
• The body can be broken down into **several tissue types**, such as** water, fat, connective tissue, muscle, bone, etc.**
 
• The **human body **is made up of hundreds of different types of **cells**, yet surprisingly, **bacteria **found in the typical human **gastrointestinal tract **make up the majority of cells (albeit not the total mass) in a person's body.
